# R-GPT: The LLM-Powered Shiny Sandbox

A Shiny app that turns plain-English requests into R code (plots, tables, summaries) using LLMs via `ellmer`, then runs and displays the result. It works on simulated CDISC data (ADSL, ADAE, ADTTE from `random.cdisc.data`) or on your own uploaded dataset (.rds, .csv, .xpt, .sas7bdat).


## Features
- Choose an model (only Gemini at the moment has a free API key)
- Simulate ADSL / ADAE / ADTTE data, or upload your own (refer to them as user_data if needed)
- Ask for tables (i.e. gt, gtsummary), plots (ggplot2, plotly, survminer) or console output
- Refine results iteratively, with an Undo button to restore previous results

## Setup
1. Install the packages used by the app (see `renv.lock` if you use renv).
2. Set your Gemini API key as an environment variable. Never put it in the code:
```r
   Sys.setenv(GOOGLE_API_KEY = "your-key")   # or add it to ~/.Renviron
```
3. Run `shiny::runApp()`.

## Example prompts
- "Kaplan-Meier plot of OS by ARM using adtte"
- "Demographics table by ARM using adsl"

## Warning
The app runs LLM-generated code with `eval()`. Use it locally, and don't expose it publicly without sandboxing.
